It deliberately asserts no derived identity: the timestamp, the committed base, the continuation harness digest, both plan hashes and the price are computed by scripts/autoinit/issue_recovery_continuation_authorization.py, which refuses a grant that claims any of them. Consumed by exactly one issuance. The attempt-4 grant and its authorization are SPENT and must not be reused: the memory-contract repairs moved BOTH the session commit and the continuation harness digest, so that artifact refuses this tree twice over.
granted_by: Maintainer decision, 2026-08-23. 'GO for Recovery Continuation Attempt 5. I reviewed c3116f2. Both Attempt-4 memory-contract blockers are closed sufficiently for one further paid continuation. The release lifecycle is now correct: the owning frame snapshots CUDA state, explicitly drops teacher and evaluator, and only then calls complete_release(before). require_released() makes genuine live retention fail closed before recovery. Keep that contract unchanged. The new RECOVERY_TRAINER_BYTES basis is also accepted. The 39.79 GiB peak comes from completed 1023-step runs of the same memory-relevant recovery recipe on an L40S under the same /opt/train torch 2.11.0+cu128 environment used by the continuation. The Attempt-4 reserved and non-PyTorch terms convert that observed PyTorch peak into the 41.65 GiB device requirement, and the existing 2 GiB headroom margin remains intact.' Against last tested implementation c3116f2, which is also the pre-authorization HEAD. Since attempt 4, two closures landed and were accepted, both inside the 22-file harness. (1) THE HANDOFF LIFECYCLE: release_to_subprocess(drop=[...]) was itself the defect -- it copied the caller's sequence into a callee-local list and cleared that, which cannot rebind a caller's name, and it measured `after` before the caller's del ran, so a real release could not register. complete_release(before) now accepts NO objects; the caller snapshots with cuda_memory(), deletes its own names, then measures. Applied identically to the continuation's teacher/evaluator path and full Phase A's found path, with `evaluator` in the del because StateEvaluator.prime_reference stores the teacher on _teacher. require_released() makes the live_retention verdict block above the same 1 GiB limit, kept separate from require_headroom so a caller can tell whether the release failed or the card is merely full. (2) THE TRAINER REQUIREMENT: RECOVERY_TRAINER_BYTES was 22 GiB, chosen from attempt 12's mid-failure footprint and 17.79 GiB below the trainer's real peak. Attempt 4's 36.30 GiB is only a lower bound because it OOM'd inside the first kd_forward_kl, before backward() and before the first AdamW.step(). The permanent controls preflight_ctl_r0860k_{sa,sb} each report max_memory_allocated() of 39.79 GiB over COMPLETED 1023-step runs on an L40S, reproducing every memory-relevant field of the frozen recipe. Converted to a device requirement with attempt 4's own reserved and non-PyTorch terms: 41.65 GiB. No calibration launch was purchased. Verified at $0 on the current tree: full suite 2172 passed / 12 skipped, +10 on 2162 with the skip count unchanged; frozen-asset verifier passed with no problems; 7 mutations each turning a passing state into a failing one. The continuation harness digest moved 162c09ed -> 95cf336d.

fail_closed_instruction: A refusal by require_released() or require_headroom() after Stage 1 is the INTENDED RESULT of this repair, not a failure of the run: preserve the evidence, fail closed, obtain provider-confirmed teardown and return for review. Do not weaken either gate, do not alter the frozen recovery recipe, and do not repair or relaunch on the live pod. On any other failure the same applies: preserve the full traceback and stage artifacts, collect evidence through the supported path, tear down with provider confirmation, and stop. The five imported Stage-1 leaves are session INPUTS: they are not re-derived, not modified, and their canonical off-pod copies in the dev-box checkpoint store remain the durable record regardless of what happens in Stages 2-5.
on_completion: Report rung-1 results, rung-2 results, whether the conditional seed-sc rung fired, the final selection, retained artifacts, actual spend and provider-confirmed teardown, together with commits and hashes, authorization identity, bundle round-trip and pod lifecycle. Tear the pod down as soon as the run reaches a terminal state rather than waiting for a backstop, and confirm teardown with the provider. Then STOP. Do not self-authorize any subsequent session.
